_about: P11 evaluation corpus. EVERY DOCUMENT IS INVENTED for testing (CC0-1.0); none is a real paper and no figure is a real measurement. Terminology is varied on purpose (capacity fade / capacity loss, swelling / volume expansion, sparsification / sparse updates) so paraphrase queries are possible. Pairs bat4/bat5 and soil1/soil2 conflict on purpose; dup1 is a near-copy of bat1.

docs.title: Silicon anode volume expansion during cycling
docs.text:
Abstract

Silicon anodes store far more lithium than graphite but undergo large volume expansion during cycling. We measured the thickness growth of silicon anodes in thirty pouch cells.

1. Methods

Each cell was cycled between 3.0 and 4.2 volts at a rate of C/3. Thickness was recorded with a dial gauge after every fifty cycles.

2. Results

Silicon anode volume expansion reached 18 percent after two hundred cycles, and capacity fell by 22 percent over the same period. Uncoated cells expanded more than cells with a carbon coating.

3. Limitations

Only one cell format was tested and calendar effects were not separated from cycling effects.

docs.title: Carbon coating reduces swelling of silicon electrodes
docs.text:
Abstract

A thin carbon coating limits the swelling of silicon electrodes. We compared coated and uncoated electrodes over repeated charge cycles.

1. Results

The carbon coating halved electrode swelling, from 18 percent to 9 percent after two hundred cycles. Capacity retention improved from 78 percent to 91 percent.

2. Limitations

Coating thickness was not varied, so the optimum thickness is unknown.

docs.title: Capacity fade of cells stored at elevated temperature
docs.text:
Abstract

Capacity loss during storage depends on temperature. We stored charged cells at 25, 35 and 45 degrees Celsius for twelve months.

1. Results

Capacity fade averaged 0.5 percent per month at 25 degrees and 3 percent per month at 45 degrees. Degradation accelerated with state of charge.

2. Limitations

Cells came from a single manufacturer and no cycling was performed.

docs.title: Fluoroethylene carbonate additive and fast charging
docs.text:
Abstract

We tested a fluoroethylene carbonate electrolyte additive under fast charging at 3C.

1. Results

The additive improved capacity retention by twelve percentage points after three hundred fast charge cycles. Cells with the additive formed a thinner interface layer.

2. Limitations

Only one additive concentration was evaluated.

docs.title: Additive-free electrolyte shows no benefit at fast charge
docs.text:
Abstract

We repeated fast charging tests at 3C with and without a fluoroethylene carbonate additive.

1. Results

The additive gave no significant difference in capacity retention after three hundred fast charge cycles. Interface layer thickness was similar with and without the additive.

2. Limitations

The cells used a different cathode chemistry from earlier reports.

docs.title: Thermal stress and coral bleaching thresholds
docs.text:
Abstract

Coral bleaching follows accumulated heat stress. We related bleaching to degree heating weeks at twelve reefs.

1. Results

Bleaching became widespread once degree heating weeks exceeded four. Reefs with variable temperature bleached less severely.

2. Limitations

Surveys were visual and depth was not controlled.

docs.title: Larval settlement on rubble substrate
docs.text:
Abstract

Settlement of coral larvae depends on the substrate. We offered larvae rubble, bare rock and sand in tanks.

1. Results

Larval settlement was highest on rubble, with twice as many recruits as on bare rock. Almost no larvae settled on sand.

2. Limitations

Tank conditions may not reflect reef currents.

docs.title: Ocean acidification and skeletal density
docs.text:
Abstract

Lower aragonite saturation limits calcification. We grew coral fragments under three acidification levels.

1. Results

Skeleton density decreased by eight percent at the lowest aragonite saturation. Growth rate fell by twelve percent.

2. Limitations

The experiment lasted only ten weeks.

docs.title: Heat tolerant symbionts and recovery after bleaching
docs.text:
Abstract

Corals hosting heat tolerant zooxanthellae may recover faster after thermal stress. We followed bleached colonies for a year.

1. Results

Colonies hosting Durusdinium regained colour in half the time of colonies hosting other symbionts. Mortality was lower in the heat tolerant group.

2. Limitations

Symbiont identity was determined for a subset of colonies only.

docs.title: Biochar amendment raises crop yield
docs.text:
Abstract

Biochar is proposed as a soil amendment. We applied biochar to loam soil in a three year field trial.

1. Results

Biochar increased maize yield by fourteen percent compared with untreated plots. Soil organic carbon also increased.

2. Limitations

Only loam soil was tested.

docs.title: Biochar application lowers yield in sandy soils
docs.text:
Abstract

We tested biochar on sandy soils in a two year field trial.

1. Results

Biochar decreased maize yield by six percent compared with untreated plots. Nitrogen availability fell after application.

2. Limitations

Biochar feedstock differed from earlier trials.

docs.title: Mycorrhizal inoculation and phosphorus uptake
docs.text:
Abstract

Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi can improve nutrient uptake. We inoculated wheat seedlings and measured phosphorus content.

1. Results

Mycorrhizal inoculation increased phosphorus uptake by twenty percent. Benefits vanished at high phosphorus supply.

2. Limitations

Plants were grown in pots, not fields.

docs.title: Legume rotation and soil nitrogen
docs.text:
Abstract

Rotating legumes with cereals may restore soil nitrogen. We measured nitrogen after three rotation cycles.

1. Results

Soil nitrogen increased by nine percent after a legume rotation compared with continuous cereal. Following cereal yield rose by seven percent.

2. Limitations

No fertiliser comparison was made.

docs.title: Client drift in federated learning with non-iid data
docs.text:
Abstract

When client data are not independent and identically distributed, local updates drift apart. We studied client drift as the number of local epochs grows.

1. Results

Client drift grew with the number of local epochs, and global accuracy fell by seven points at twenty local epochs.

2. Limitations

Only image classification tasks were studied.

docs.title: Gradient compression with top-k sparsification
docs.text:
Abstract

Uploading full gradients is expensive. We applied top-k sparsification to client gradients.

1. Results

Top-k sparsification cut the bytes per round by ninety percent while accuracy dropped by one point.

2. Limitations

Compression error accumulated on slow networks.

docs.title: Differential privacy noise in federated training
docs.text:
Abstract

Privacy requires clipping and gaussian noise. We trained with several privacy budgets epsilon.

1. Results

A smaller privacy budget epsilon needed more noise and accuracy fell by five points at epsilon one.

2. Limitations

Only one clipping norm was explored.

docs.title: Communication efficient training with sparse updates
docs.text:
Abstract

Sending sparse model updates reduces the upload volume of each client. We evaluated sparse updates against dense updates.

1. Results

Sparse updates reduced upload volume by eighty five percent and final accuracy changed by less than one point.

2. Limitations

Network delay was simulated rather than measured.
